newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end down on profit taking, rates.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end down on profit taking, rates.

text.p: Toronto stocks finished lower on Thursday, depressed by profit taking and continued fears of a hike in U.S. interest rates next week.
The TSE 300 Composite Index fell 33.68 points to close at 6055.28, its fourth straight losing session this week.
Trading was active with 82 million shares changing hands worth C$1.27 billion ($920 million).
Earlier today, U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan signalled the Fed may raise rates next week as a preemptive move to keep inflation low.
Aside from rate jitters, Canada's biggest stock market was also hit by profit takers, analysts said.

"Toronto is not coming off just because of Mr. Greenspan. Our interest sensitive stocks and the banks have had enormous runs and it is the most likely place for profit taking," said Montreal-based equity strategist Bill Ram.
He said the market was expecting a "mild bump" in U.S. rates after next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
"But I think the expectation is (Greenspan) is not going to raise rates just to bring the market down. It hasn't been his style in the past and I don't think it is now," Ram said.
All but two of Toronto's 14 sectors lost ground. Declining stocks outpaced advances 567 to 393 with 287 issues unchanged.

* Takeover target Wascana Energy Inc. topped the actives list, adding 0.10 to 20.65 on 2.7 million shares. Wascana agreed to a C$2 billion ($1.4 billion) friendly bid from Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd. earlier this week. CanOxy slipped 0.30 to 25.95 on 890,000 shares.
* Among rate sensitive stocks, Royal Bank of Canada fell 0.35 to 55.90 on 978,000 shares. BCE Inc. dropped 0.45 to 63.70 on 606,000 shares.

* United Grain Growers Ltd. gained 0.95 to 12.75 after the company's board decided to postpone its poison pill indefinitely. Two Canadian wheat pools dropped their hostile bid for UGG this week after a Canadian court ruled against their bid to have the pill removed.
